items.title: Mapping the microbes' arms race with viruses at planetary scale
items.summary: Microbiomes are complex ecosystems, in which bacteria and archaea are constantly interacting with, and infected by, viruses. These viruses can significantly impact microbiome processes, not only by killing their host but also sometimes by temporarily providing additional capabilities to their host. As many viruses have not been grown in a lab, connecting them to their natural hosts has been difficult. A new bioinformatics toolkit and database are now available to help researchers make those associations at an unprecedented scale.

Researchers have found that a blood test used for Alzheimer's can also detect a protein fragment that points to CTE. It can develop into addiction, psychosis and violence, and has been linked to higher risk of ALS .

MLB seeks to redistribute player compensation within the league. While the union and league battle over the future of baseball's economics and are barreling toward a management lockout, a lesser-known element also lies at the heart of MLB's vision of the future. Team owners want to change the current separation between player compensation and their on-field value. According to MLB research presented this week to reporters, players with six years or fewer of major league service and not eligible for free agency delivered 71% of the league's total on-field value, as measured by wins over replacement (WAR). That group, however, received just 31% of the total compensation.

An Orange County legal court puts Fens on the basketball court, for now. Today's hearing in front of Judge Alyson Grine sought a Temporary Restraining Order (TRO), a legal mechanism now familiar to most college sports fans. A TRO grants one party in a lawsuit temporary relief while a legal argument proceeds in court. The basic idea is that a party suffering harm while the lawsuit unfolds cannot recover that harm even if he or she wins their case. In other words, Fens' lawyers today argued that Fens' suit has enough merit to be successful but that missing games now irreparably harms him. Those games can't be given back if he wins his suit in a few months.

The ability to detect CTE only through autopsies prevents football players from knowing whether they have it during their careers. Via ESPN, a pair of studies published by The Journal of the American Medical Association show that a new blood test could detect advanced stages of CTE in a living patient. A study from Boston University and Banner Health was based on blood drawn from a small sample of former players during their lifetimes. Autopsies performed after they died showed that they had CTE. The researchers then found a marker for CTE based on the levels of a specific type of protein in their blood.

A 15-inch golf grip killed a nasty duck hook. Per MyGolfSpy, the JumboMax Ultralong fixed the swing with less pressure and more touchpoints. The theory behind the grip is simple. A bigger grip helps a player hold on with less pressure. This lowers tension in the forearms and softens the hands. That change improves tempo and quiets overactive wrists. JumboMax President and founder John Mazzanoble told MyGolfSpy , "Our fitting process is a five-step process." Currently, CTE can only be detected after someone has died. As of now, CTE can be diagnosed only after death , through direct study and dissection of the brain. However, two studies published this week in the Journal of the American Medical Association (JAMA) both point to the possibility of detecting CTE through blood tests. The first study was published by a research group with the Washington University School of Medicine on Nov. 13; the second , from researchers at Boston University and Banner Health, was published Thursday. Both indicate the presence of biomarkers in the blood that correlate with the presence of CTE.

The Irish League's most successful manager Roy Coyle has died at the age of 80. Roy Coyle, the most successful manager in Irish League history, has died at the age of 80. Coyle won 13 league titles during his 32-year managerial career, achieving periods of sustained success with Linfield and Glentoran. He moved into management at 29 when he was appointed player-manager of Linfield in November 1975. A midfielder during his playing days, Coyle had spells with the Glens, Sheffield Wednesday, Grimsby Town and Linfield after starting out with Ballymena United, and he also won five caps for Northern Ireland.

Microsoft Outlook security flaw CVE-2026-124194 lets hackers steal NTLMv2 authentication data through malicious files. Microsoft confirms attacks are underway. Formula 1 will begin introducing full-time stewards in 2027, in a move designed to bring greater continuity to race officiating. But the FIA’s announcement is not a promise that controversial decisions will vanish overnight. The governing body says it will recruit a small number of experienced international stewards for a phased introduction next season. The long-term target is a department of 12 to 15 full-time officials, with the group expected to expand from 2028 onwards. Existing part-time stewards will remain involved, and the FIA says driver stewards will continue to contribute their specialist experience at events.

Willie Burton played in the NBA for eight seasons, spending only three games with the Charlotte Hornets during the 1998-99 season. After spending time overseas, Burton played with both Hawks and Spurs before joining the Charlotte Hornets ahead of the 1998-99 campaign. Burton's tenure with the Hornets lasted only three games, where he averaged 1.3 points and two rebounds before being waived. In 316 games over eight seasons, Burton left the NBA with career averages of 10.3 points, 2.9 rebounds, 1.2 assists and 0.6 steals. He would go on to play professionally in the United States and overseas until ending his career after the 2003-04 season.

Stephen Curry's absence has caused a shocking 26.8-point swing in Golden State's average scoring margin this season. Through 16 games, the Warriors have averaged 118.6 points in Curry's ten appearances while allowing 109.5, which produces a plus-9.1 scoring margin. FCC preempts state rules that require AT&T to keep offering home phone service. AT&T’s status as a Carrier of Last Resort in California requires it to offer telephone service to any potential customer in its territory. AT&T wants to stop offering basic phone service to new customers and discontinue service for 184,000 residential customers and 15,000 business customers on June 1, 2027. The order released today granted AT&T’s request to preempt state rules, following up on the FCC’s previous approval of AT&T’s petition to discontinue service. AT&T had tried to achieve the same result in court, but a federal judge rejected its request to override California’s rules in July.

The Common Cents Act established guidelines for businesses and consumers when conducting cash transactions. President Trump on Friday signed the Common Cents Act , which lets businesses round cash transactions to the nearest nickel, into law. It sets standards for cash transactions that businesses and consumers can use when exact change isn't available, as the penny is phased out. The legislation calls for cash transactions to be rounded up or down to the nearest 5 cents. For example, if a purchase costs $10.02 after tax and a customer is short 2 cents, the tab would round down to $10 under the act. A charge of $10.04 would round up to $10.05.
